To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a crack in a conductor can be detected by an eddy current coil, and that the impedance of the coil is a function of crack size and shape.

1) the impedance variation of a coil in the vicinity of a crack in a conductor can be computed accurately using a boundary element formulation; 2) the impedance change due to a slot is larger than that of an ideal crack; 3) the impedance change of an ideal crack is proportional to the crack length; 4) the coil impedance change is proportional to the square of the coil diameter; 5) the coil impedance changes with the coil orientation relative to the crack; and
the coil impedance variation due to a crack in a hole can be predicted with reasonable accuracy using a boundary integral formulation of the eddy-current problem.

the development of a theoretical and computational framework for the analysis of the eddy current response of cracks in fastener holes.
the development of theoretical and computational models that predict the signals due to defects in fastener holes using eddy-current probe signals.
